# requireNonFunction

<link-summary>Returns the value after checking that it is not a function.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNonFunction() — Returns the value after checking that it is not a function. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNonFunction<T>( value: T, message: string = "Expected a non-function value." // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-function-type ): Exclude<T, Function>;
```

Classified by its internal tag, so ordinary, `async`, generator and async-generator functions all pass. A class is a function too.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                   | Type     | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------------------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                     | `T`      | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a non-function value."` | `string` | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`Exclude<T, Function>` — the same value, with a function excluded from its type.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is a function. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNonFunction(null); // => null
requireNonFunction("fn"); // => "fn"
requireNonFunction(function () {}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonFunction(async function () {}); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
